title: Finite coproduct comparison for Cech complexes over an etale object
statement: Let X be a scheme, U an object of its small etale category, I a finite type in Type (u+1), V_i etale X-schemes with arrows f_i to U. Let W be an etale X-scheme with g:W→U and c_i:V_i→W, whose underlying scheme cofan is a coproduct and c_i followed by g equals f_i. For every abelian sheaf G on X_et, the Mathlib Cech complexes in Over U for (f_i) and the singleton (g) with the restricted G are isomorphic. No covering or affineness hypothesis is imposed. [def-weil-pbc-cech-complex] [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]

source.place: Tag 03OZ, equation 59.22.1.1 and the fibre-product coproduct formula in the proof; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03OZ

proof.text: Use the canonical Pi.map arrows in Over U. The new geometric product-cofan theorem identifies their underlying scheme cofan as a coproduct, by transporting the existing fibre-product distribution through Etale.overEquiv and finite-product comparisons.

For any finite scheme coproduct cofan in X_et, Sigma.desc of its arrows is an isomorphism. Its inclusions are open immersions by Sigma.ι_desc, their images cover by sigmaOpenCover and surjectivity, and are disjoint by injectivity and sigmaι_eq_iff. Faithfulness of the forgetful functor gives monicity in X_et. Apply the already proved Etale.isIso_piLift_of_disjoint. This proves the product restriction map is an isomorphism, including empty tuple families.

Construct the cosimplicial restriction transformation directly between Mathlib formal-coproduct cosimplicial objects. In each degree its components are the singleton-tuple product projection followed by restriction along Pi.map of the c_i. Naturality follows after each target projection from Pi.map_π and Pi.lift_π: deleting or repeating a factor commutes with applying the same coprojections. Functor.map_comp transfers these equalities to sections. The singleton-tuple projection is the productUniqueIso hom; composing it with step 2 proves each component is an isomorphism. Apply Mathlib alternatingCofaceMapComplex to get a chain map, HomologicalComplex.Hom.isIso_of_components to make it invertible, and take its inverse to obtain the required orientation.

theorem nonempty_etale_over_coproduct_cech_iso
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Etale) (I : Type (u + 1)) [Finite I]
    (V : I → X.Etale) (f : ∀ i : I, V i ⟶ U)
    (W : X.Etale) (g : W ⟶ U) (c : ∀ i : I, V i ⟶ W)
    (hc : IsColimit (Cofan.mk W.left (fun i ↦ (c i).left)))
    (hw : ∀ i : I, c i ≫ g = f i)
    (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
    Nonempty (((cechComplexFunctor fun i : I ↦ Over.mk (f i)).obj
      ((Over.forget U).op ⋙ G.obj)) ≅
      ((cechComplexFunctor fun _ : Fin 1 ↦ Over.mk g).obj
        ((Over.forget U).op ⋙ G.obj)))
